target_customer: Traders, liquidity providers and developers in the Bittensor (TAO) ecosystem
problem: Bittensor had little DeFi infrastructure, so holders could not easily swap, bridge, stake or borrow against TAO and subnet tokens.
business_model: Decentralised exchange fees and protocol revenue on the Bittensor EVM

founders.name: Sam Forman
founders.background_notes: Only founder named on the YC page; no background given.

technical_complexity.rationale: The later product was a Uniswap style concentrated liquidity exchange plus bridges on Bittensor's EVM, which relied on existing DeFi patterns but needed bridge security.

defensibility.rationale: DEX code is open and copyable; early position and ecosystem ties to Bittensor helped but did not lock in users.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbents were building DeFi for Bittensor when the product launched; the company was bought by a London listed firm in January 2026.

market_need_then: At the 2021 YC batch no source describes TaoFi's demand. The documented need is from 2024 and 2025, when Bittensor added EVM smart contracts and subnet tokens needed trading venues.

branding.domain_note: Owns taofi.com, which carries a Swap page for the product.

rebrands.why: One crypto news item says the acquirer rebranded it; seen in a single source, unverified.

branding.community_and_virality: Covered in Bittensor ecosystem media (TaoDaily, Bankless, Hyperlane blog), indicating community attention inside that niche.

brand_strength.rationale: Recognised within the Bittensor community as the main early DeFi venue, but no wider brand evidence.

outcome_analysis: TaoFi became a DeFi layer for the Bittensor ecosystem and raised a strategic round led by DCG with Pantera in February 2025, riding the growth in subnet tokens after Bittensor added EVM support. It was then acquired by Astrid Intelligence plc in January 2026 for shares at an undisclosed value, so it exited within a niche ecosystem rather than a broad market.
notes: YC lists batch Winter 2021 and founding 2020, but every source found about the product dates from 2024 to 2025; what the company did in 2020 to 2021 and when it moved to Bittensor is not documented, so no pivot is recorded. Round amount not disclosed. Acquisition terms: one report says all share consideration, announced 20 January 2026; value undisclosed. Rebrand to Astrid Bridge is single source. No dated 2021 competitor source exists; competitors left empty. Brand search found nothing about a mascot or logo.
